correctness.rationale: For strictly positive substrate, free enzyme, binding and catalytic parameters (and nonnegative dissociation), the two equilibrium LNAs have explicitly derived stable drift and diffusion matrices. Their exactly inverted substrate PSDs differ by a rational function with numerator -d ω⁴+B ω²+C₀, B,C₀>0, and strictly positive denominators. A concave quadratic in squared frequency has precisely one positive zero if d>0 and no nonnegative zero if d=0. This analytically proves the complete sign classification; a separate symbolic residual check is exactly zero, 1,200 independently constructed resolvent checks and 100 independent covariance-Lyapunov checks yielded 5,000 successful numerical comparisons.

originality.rationale: The 2011 Thomas–Straube–Grima source gives an integrated substrate-variance overestimate, not a signed frequency-local full-LNA/hQSSA auto-spectrum comparison. The 2012 article provides spectral resolvent methodology and slow-scale reduction, not the all-parameter unique-crossing theorem. The 2025 Marmolejo Lozano–Popović–Grima paper provides general spectra and analyses substrate–product coherence/MI in an extended network, not an explicit substrate auto-spectrum sign reversal, uniqueness cutoff, or dissociation-zero exception. The signed rational factorization and positivity arguments are additional to these premises, rather than a mere restatement of any inspected prior conclusion. Claim of historical priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The natural, previously published biochemical question was whether stochastic-QSSA variance estimates are faithful. The exact signed spectral result strengthens that context in a materially distinct direction: an integrated overestimate hides a unique high-frequency underestimate when dissociation is positive. It yields an explicit physically interpretable crossover and the sharp k1=0 boundary, identifying which frequency ranges can be biased in opposite directions. That information is relevant to frequency-resolved fluctuation measurements and to diagnosing the limits of reduced biochemical kinetics, while carefully delimiting the high-frequency physical validity of the Gaussian models.
